# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

content.thinking:
I need to account for the directory_external_show setting gating external rows, plus the live blocklist re-check against host suffixes and PTR names, which is hard to push fully into SQL. My plan is to query stored verdicts for paging, then re-apply the live rule set on the page of 24 as a safety net per spec, though that means SQL GROUP BY counts could mismatch rows the live rules would block but the stored verdict didn't catch.

I'm avoiding a schema migration entirely by skipping new columns — instead computing the shortId as a hash of connKey at read time. Since sha1 isn't built into Postgres but sha256 is (PG11+), I'll use sha256 truncated to 10 hex characters scoped by game for lookups, which is cheap enough without an index given each game has only a few thousand rows; I'm now checking whether connKey is actually unique per row, since source+sourceKey is unique but connKey is only indexed, so multiple sources could share one.

For continent filtering, I'm mapping countries to continents in JS and letting SQL just filter on country lists, then grouping by upper(country) for facet counts — no extra column needed. Given the current row counts (6k, scaling to maybe 20-60k), I'm skipping the spec'd DirectoryFacetCache table and migration in favor of a simple in-process TTL cache, relying on the existing (game, hidden, lastSeenAt) index to keep sorted/filtered queries fast enough without new indexes.

For pagination I'll go with offset-based numbered pages capped at a max (e.g. 200) for crawlability, rather than keyset pagination. Sorting options will cover players (desc, nulls last, then name), newest, and name — skipping "fullest" and "ping" since ping requires client geolocation, which I may handle separately via country-based proximity.

For filters, I'm planning country and continent scoping, a players has/notfull toggle, a simple ILIKE name search without trigram indexing (acceptable at this scale), and an Nxeon-only flag. I'm second-guessing whether game-specific tag parsing belongs in this phase or was explicitly excluded by the caller's scope, since it overlaps with descriptions and A2S_RULES work that's meant to come later.

Cards shouldn't show raw tags or a literal "Map:" label, so I'm thinking a map-name chip is acceptable styling-wise. For the detail page's About section, I'll derive a minimal factual fallback line purely from stored fields (game, country, map, slot count) without needing parsed tags at all, and player counts will only display when the live data is fresh within the last 60 minutes.

For aggregating "players playing," I should only sum counts from listings with a recent lastSeenAt timestamp. For indexability thresholds, region pages need roughly 10 real listings per the owner's brief, while game pages must still render an honest empty state with noindex when there's no data yet — so I'm settling on a similar ~10-row threshold for marking a game page indexable, even though the existing check only required 3.

I'm still weighing game vs region thresholds — maybe 5 for games since the page has richer content (host CTA, region links, FAQ) versus 10 for regions, though I could just keep both at 10 for simplicity; I'll pick 5 and leave it as an easily adjustable constant. I also need to confirm external rows only render when the directory_external_show flag is true, which seems to be the case in prod since the live page showed 602 entries, and note that the NXM_LIVE flag controls robots behavior.

For the "near you" geo logic, I'm checking how country gets derived from the request — since these pages are force-dynamic already, I can compute location server-side in the page itself rather than client-fetching it, even though the spec hints at client-side fetching for ISR; the tradeoff is a crawler hitting from the US would just see US results, which seems acceptable. The card grid renders as plain HTML with no JSON payload, which is good. For server detail pages, I'm now figuring out the URL pattern and whether Nxeon-hosted paid entries get their own detail pages at all, since free MC and community servers have distinct href patterns while paid Nxeon entries currently have none.

For paid Nxeon entries I'm deciding to give them detail pages using a hashed id derived from their internal key (prefixed to avoid exposing anything sensitive), while free/community Nxeon entries keep linking to their existing pages instead of getting a new directory detail page — only the paid ones need lookup-and-hash treatment, and I'm satisfied that's indexable. other `/opt/dayz/serverfiles` (script)
backups `/var/backups/nxeon-game` (script, created later) | from-setup-script | | fivem | `/opt/fivem/server-data` | mods `/opt/fivem/server-data/resources` (script)
config `/opt/fivem/server-data` (script)
backups `/var/backups/nxeon-game` (script, created later) | from-setup-script | ### Files tab polish and the folder-open delay (2026-10-05) Shared file browser (`components/customer/files/*`, used by VPS and game servers; `HostingFilesPanel` has its own component and is untouched). **Root cause of "there is a slight delay".** Measured against four real running servers (read-only, directory names only): the listing itself takes 2-5 ms. Every folder click paid a brand-new SSH connection (TCP + key exchange + auth + SFTP subsystem, 150-350 ms, up to ~1 s on a cold path) because `withSftp` opened and closed one per call; on top of that every decrypt of the root password and the management key ran `scryptSync` (~35 ms of blocking CPU each, so ~70 ms of event-loop stall per click; `lib/crypto-box.ts` now memoises the derived key). The game-folder fallback made it worse: the browser probed the landing folder, then each parent, one request and one SSH handshake at a time, then listed again (0.6-1.1 s for a missing folder). **Fixes.** (1) `lib/sftp-pool.ts`: a keyed, idle-expiring connection pool used only by READ operations (list, read). Key = authenticated user id + server id + target host:port + credential fingerprint, so a connection is never handed to another user or server and is abandoned when the credential rotates; every call still runs the session, ownership, throttle and path checks first (the pool only saves the handshake); idle timeout 25 s, at most 32 connections (oldest idle evicted), closed on `close`/`end`/`error`, evicted on a connection-type error (one retry on a fresh connection), operations on one connection serialised. (2) `listFilesNearest` / `listNearestDir`: the missing-folder fallback is ONE call on one connection. (3) Client: navigation is optimistic (path and path bar update at once), a per-mount stale-while-revalidate listing cache (`lib/files-nav.ts` `ListingCache`, keyed by source + canonical path, cleared on every write), hover/focus prefetch (150 ms rest, at most one per 400 ms, cancelled on leave), a double-click guard, spinner + "Opening..." on the pressed control, an aria-live announcement, an inline error with Retry, the NX preloader (`NxLoaderMark`, reused from `components/nx/Preloader.tsx`) above "Reading ..." when a NEW folder with no cached listing is opened, and a persistent path bar (full absolute path, copy button, "Game files > ..." label). | Server (real, running) | Per click today (unpooled median) | Pooled, warm | Pooled first call | Missing-folder walk, old | Missing-folder walk, new | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Minecraft Paper | 276 ms | 1 ms | 163 ms | 721-999 ms | 4 ms | | Palworld | 253 ms | 1 ms | 160 ms | 672-991 ms | 4 ms | | Project Zomboid | 195 ms | 1 ms | 149 ms | 651-739 ms | 6 ms | | Valheim (BepInEx) | 241 ms | 1 ms | 156 ms | 621-1122 ms | 5 ms | (Unpooled and the first pooled call include the SSH handshake; "warm" is the server-side function only, add one browser to server round trip. The unpooled figures drop by ~70-80 ms after the scrypt memo; the table shows the numbers before it for the first column and after it for the pooled columns.) ## Server directory: Steam region fan-out (2026-10-05) Why: the Steam list answers "nearest to the requester" and our requester is the Singapore primary, so one unfiltered request per game came back ~100% Asia-Pacific. - **Ingest** (`lib/directory-ingest/valve.ts` `fetchValveList`): one `GetServerList` request per Steam region code (0 US East, 1 US West, 2 South America, 3 Europe, 4 Asia, 5 Oceania, 6 Middle East, 7 Africa; 255 = world), sequential with a 750 ms pause, 300 rows per region (`limit`/`perRegionLimit`), merged and de-duplicated by `sourceKey`. Any failed region request throws `ValveFetchError`, so the game fails as one unit and backoff/breaker work as before. `regions: [255]` (CLI `--regions 255`) restores the old single worldwide request. - **Budget**: the sweep counts every real HTTP request (the ingest calls `onRequest` just before each send, so a game that fails on region 4 is charged 4). A game is only started when the remaining day budget covers all its regions. A game costs 8 calls; 11 games at the default hourly schedule is about 1,700 calls/day. `STEAM_DAILY_CALL_CAP` is now 4000 (4% of Valve's 100,000; the key is shared with the Workshop sync). `MAX_GAMES_PER_TICK` stays 2 (a tick is at most 16 requests, about 12 s). - **Shrink guard / prune** unchanged: the first multi-region run grows the set, which is never "suspicious"; collapsing back to one region would be, and then nothing is pruned. - **Country at ingest** (`lib/directory-ingest/geo.ts`): new rows (and rows with no country) get an ISO-2 country from the bundled geoip-lite dataset. Optional (`geo: false` disables), never fails ingest, never overwrites a stored country (so `/root/nxeon-directory-locate.py` results win). geoip-lite must stay in `serverExternalPackages`. No schema change: the Steam region code is only an in-memory hint (`steamRegion`). - **Display**: `externalEntries` reads up to 400 rows per continent bucket (plus one for rows with no/unknown country; continent from `lib/geo-continent.ts`), applies the blocklist/liveness filters, then picks at most `EXTERNAL_TOTAL` (1000) with an even share per continent (surplus from small continents is redistributed; best-by-players first inside each). Public game pages (`/game-servers/directory/`) do the same for their 120 cards after the Nxeon-hosted ones. The portal "All regions" select now lists continents that exist in the data plus the countries/locations present. Portal payload: about 447 bytes per row, so 600 rows (before) ~268 KB, up to 1000 rows (after) ~447 KB of RSC data before gzip. - Operator note: until the next sweep fills the new regions, and until rows have a country, the other continents are empty or sit in the "unknown" bucket. 19191:## Mod install coverage + honest Mods tab (2026-10-02, branch `fix/mod-install-coverage`) 19427:## Saved-card health sweep (added 2026-10-05) 19443:## AI agent hosting hub: /ai-agents (2026-10-04, branch feature/ai-agents-hosting, not deployed) 19528:## Game files on the customer Files tab (2026-10-05) 19612:## Server directory: Steam region fan-out (2026-10-05)

## Server directory v2: aggregate pages (2026-10-05, branch `feature/directory-hub`)

Phase 2 of `/root/agent-notes/directory-overhaul/SPEC.md` (the aggregate pages), built on `feature/directory-regions`. Behind **Setting `directory_v2_enabled`** (default off; switch on `/admin/directory`, "New directory pages (v2)"). Off = the v1 single page exactly as before, and the new URLs 404.

**Routes** (NXM site; served at the real URLs through the `NXM_ROOT` middleware rewrite; new pattern `^/game-servers/directory/[^/]+/[^/]+$` in `scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts` / `app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json`):

| URL | What | Indexed |
|---|---|---|
| `/game-servers/directory` | home: search, near you (visitor country from the geo header / offline geoip, never stored), Hosted on Nxeon shelf (hidden when empty), game tiles by players, continents + top countries, most players now, newly listed | yes; `?q=` / `?region=` browse views are noindex, canonical to the home |
| `/game-servers/directory/games` | every `GAME_FAMILIES` key (54), counts or "No servers listed yet", "Not hosted by Nxeon" on families without an active GamePlan | yes |
| `/game-servers/directory/<game>` | region tabs + country chips with counts, GET filter form (`q`, `players=has|notfull`, `sort=newest|name`), 24 per page `?page=N`, data-derived intro, FAQ, host CTA. Works for every family, with an honest empty state | when >= `GAME_INDEX_MIN` (5) listings |
| `/game-servers/directory/<game>/<region>` | `<region>` = continent slug (`europe`, `north-america`, ...) or country slug (`germany`, `united-states`, `south-korea`) from `lib/directory-regions.ts`; ISO codes and case variants 308 to the canonical slug; unknown slugs 404. Adds a "busiest" table and region FAQ | when >= `REGION_INDEX_MIN` (10) listings |
| `/game-servers/directory/server/<game>-<10 hex>` | detail: connect box (Copy, Steam connect for Steam-list rows), players, freshness, factual "about" line from stored fields only, similar servers | only Nxeon-hosted listings; third-party = `noindex,follow` |

Page 2+ and any filtered/sorted variant: `noindex,follow` (page N keeps a self canonical, filters canonicalise to the unfiltered page). Out-of-range `?page=` 404s. JSON-LD: BreadcrumbList (from the loader trail) + CollectionPage/ItemList (first 24, production URLs) + FAQPage (from the page's own FAQ).

**Files.** Pure, unit-tested: `lib/directory-regions.ts` (slug <-> ISO table), `lib/directory-query-sql.ts` (parameterised WHERE/ORDER/LIMIT, facets GROUP BY, short-id lookup), `lib/directory-seo.ts` (facet roll-up, index rules, canonical, copy, JSON-LD, sitemap paths), `lib/directory-ids.ts` (public ids: sha256(connKey) first 10 hex; Nxeon listings sha256("nx:"+key); never a db id). Server: `lib/directory-query.ts` (SQL paging + counts, Nxeon entries merged as a pinned set, live blocklist re-check on the rendered page, in-process caches: context 30 s, facets 120 s, list pages 60 s), `app/nxm/_data/directory-hub.ts` (markup + `meta`), `lib/sitemap-directory.ts`. The template `tools/nxm/native/server-directory/body.html` is now one `{{nxm:page:html}}` slot; v1 markup is composed by `legacyPage()` in `app/nxm/_data/server-directory.ts` (byte-identical to the old body, checked). New route files `app/nxm/game-servers/directory/{games,[game]/[region],server/[id]}/page.tsx` are hand-written (outside the generator's set); the two existing generated routes are unchanged. Styles `dh-*` in the template's `page.css`; `page.js` only auto-submits the filter selects, announces copies and closes the filter panel on Esc (pages work with JS off).

**Honesty.** Counts are labelled "at the last refresh"; a player count shows only while under an hour old ("Most players" sorts by fresh counts only); cards say "Seen on the list" unless our prober answered; the Steam attribution now takes `checked` (v2 passes the prober state, so it no longer says "Nxeon checks each one directly" while the prober is off; v1 wording unchanged). Every list carries "Server details come from server owners or public server lists and may be out of date ... email abuse@nxeon.cloud".

**Sitemap.** New child `/sitemap/directory.xml` (only while v2 is on): home, all-games, indexable game and region pages, Nxeon-hosted detail pages; `<lastmod>` = newest listing's first-seen time for that page. With v2 on, `/game-servers/directory*` leaves the `games`/`servers` sections. Unknown section ids (the retired numeric `/sitemap/<n>.xml`) now 404 instead of an empty 200 urlset (`isKnownSection`, regardless of the flag).

**Performance** (throwaway Postgres, 40,153 rows, no new indexes): facets GROUP BY 85 ms (cached 2 min), one game page 6-22 ms, cross-game sorts (home shelves, search) 100-125 ms (cached 60 s). Rendered game page ~480 KB HTML in dev (~75 KB gzip) against v1's 776 KB / 90 KB gzip for 120 cards. No schema change. Suggested later (spec section 6, needs the safe-migration process): `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on `("firstSeenAt" DESC)` and `(game, players DESC NULLS LAST)` for the public set.

**Not in this phase** (owner decisions in the spec): portal twin `/dashboard/directory/...`, favourites, images pipeline, descriptions/A2S_RULES, tag parsing/facets, claim/submit, report path, new sources, prober changes.
EOF
echo done

input.message:
## Directory v2 aggregate pages: built and committed, not merged or deployed

The new directory pages work on a throwaway database with about 40k fake rows. Type check is clean and the full test suite adds no new failures. Nothing is merged to main and nothing is deployed. Prod DB and /opt/nxeon were not touched.

**Branch:** `feature/directory-hub` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-dirhub`), based on `feature/directory-regions` b61337afbe.
**Commit:** `b0fdb1d7bc`, 32 files, staged by explicit paths only (no node_modules). The message ends with the Sonnet 5.5 co-author line.

### Behind a flag
- The pages sit behind Setting `directory_v2_enabled`, default off. The spec's Phase 2 asks for that flag.
- There is a new switch on `/admin/directory`: "New directory pages (v2)".
- **Flag off:** the v1 page renders exactly as before (I checked the markup is byte-identical), and the new URLs 404.

### Routes built
All are served at the real URLs through the existing `NXM_ROOT` rewrite. I added one new pattern, `^/game-servers/directory/[^/]+/[^/]+$`, and regenerated `live-routes.json`.

| URL | What it shows | Indexed when |
|---|---|---|
| `/game-servers/directory` | Hub: search, near you (visitor's country, not stored), Nxeon-hosted shelf (hidden when empty), game tiles with counts and players, continents and top countries, most players now, newly listed | Always. `?q=` and `?region=` views are noindex, canonical to the hub |
| `/game-servers/directory/games` | All 54 games, including ones with no servers. Games without an active plan are labelled "Not hosted by Nxeon" | Always |
| `/game-servers/directory/<game>` | Region tabs and country chips with counts, GET filter form (search, players, sort), 24 per page with numbered pages, intro written from the real numbers, FAQ, host-your-own CTA. Empty games get an honest empty state | 5 or more listings |
| `/game-servers/directory/<game>/<region>` | Same as the game page for one continent or country (e.g. `europe`, `germany`). Adds a busiest-servers table and a region FAQ | 10 or more listings |
| `/game-servers/directory/server/<game>-<10hex>` | Detail: address with Copy, "Connect with Steam" for Steam-list rows, player count, freshness, an "about" line built only from stored fields, similar servers | Only for Nxeon-hosted servers. Third-party servers are noindex,follow |

- **Bad URLs:** ISO codes and wrong case (`/rust/DE`) send a permanent 308 redirect to the canonical slug. Unknown regions, games and out-of-range pages 404.
- **Page 2+ and filtered views:** noindex,follow. Page N keeps its own canonical; filtered views canonicalise to the unfiltered page.
- **Structured data:** BreadcrumbList, CollectionPage/ItemList (first 24 rows, production URLs) and FAQPage.

### How it's put together
- **Template:** I ran the generator rather than hand-editing its output. The template's `body.html` is now a single `{{nxm:page:html}}` slot. The v1 markup moved into `legacyPage()`. The two existing generated routes are unchanged; the three new route files are hand-written outside the generated set.
- **Data:** queries run in SQL with server-side paging and counts, replacing the in-memory top-N. Nxeon-hosted servers are merged in as a pinned set. The blocklist is re-checked on each rendered page.
- **No schema change.** Detail ids are computed (sha256 of the connection key) and the SQL computes the same value.
- **Visuals:** built on the existing NXM tokens (navy, violet gradient, cyan for live). Each card has a generated thumbnail: the game art tinted by a per-server colour, with the server's initials. Mobile has scrollable chips, a filter panel and 44px touch targets.

### Sitemap
- A new child, `/sitemap/directory.xml`, exists only while the flag is on. It lists only indexable pages, with `lastmod` = the newest listing's first-seen date on that page.
- With the flag on, directory URLs are removed from the `games` and `servers` sections.
- **Live as soon as merged, even with the flag off:** unknown section ids, including the old numeric `/sitemap/<n>.xml`, now return 404 instead of an empty 200.

### Honesty change
The Steam attribution text said "Nxeon checks each one directly", which isn't true while the prober is off. It now takes a `checked` option, and v2 pages pass the real prober state. The v1 default wording is unchanged, so v1 still makes that claim.

### Tests
- **New:** `test/directory-hub.test.ts` (15 tests), `test/directory-hub-render.test.ts` (5), and `test/directory-hub-db.test.ts` (4, runs only when `DIRECTORY_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set). All pass. Together with the existing directory tests that's 79 passing, 0 failing.
- **Coverage:** region slugs (uniqueness and round trip), the SQL builder (values only as parameters, LIKE escaping, paging), JS/SQL id equality, index thresholds, canonicals, copy (no "provider", no superlatives), JSON-LD shape, breadcrumbs, sitemap paths, HTML escaping, and the v1 composer.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`:** exit 0.
- **Full suite:** 3221 tests, 44 failing. All are in the 46-name baseline except one: "ptr resolver: timeout, failure, concurrency cap and lookup budget" in `directory-blocklist.test.ts`. It passed 3 out of 3 runs on its own, so I believe it's a timing flake under suite load.

### Payload and performance
Measured on a throwaway Postgres with 40,153 rows and no new indexes:

| Query | Time | Cached for |
|---|---|---|
| Facet counts (one GROUP BY) | 85 ms | 2 min |
| One game page | 6–22 ms | 60 s |
| Cross-game sorts and search (hub shelves) | 100–125 ms | 60 s |
| Detail lookup | 17 ms | — |

- **Page size:** a game page is about 480 KB of HTML (about 75 KB gzip) in the dev server. v1's 120-card page was 776 KB (90 KB gzip). Dev-server render times were 0.5–0.8 s once warm.
- **Suggested later:** two indexes created concurrently through the safe-migration process: `firstSeenAt DESC` and `(game, players DESC NULLS LAST)`.

### Things I was unsure about
- **The flag:** the brief said "live-ready" but the spec asks for this flag, so it ships off. Merging changes nothing visible except the sitemap 404.
- **Thresholds:** the game-page minimum of 5 listings was my choice (the region minimum of 10 is the owner's). Both are constants in `lib/directory-seo.ts`.
- **Removal contact:** I used `abuse@nxeon.cloud` from the spec, but I haven't checked that the mailbox exists.
- **Server names:** names like "discord.gg/…" show unfiltered. Cleaning them is the later descriptions/abuse phase.
- **Out of scope:** the portal twin (spec Phase 3), favourites, images, tag parsing, claim/report, new sources and prober changes.
- **Paid listings:** these now carry a country derived from their node's region, so they appear on region pages.

### Screenshots
`/root/agent-notes/directory-hub/`: 22 PNGs at 1440 and 390 for the hub, games, rust, rust/germany, rust/europe, palworld (empty), l4d2/africa (empty), a server detail page, a search view and `/servers` (v1, unchanged), plus a `before-` pair of the old page. Throwaway data, dev server and database are stopped and deleted.

### Steps to deploy
1. Merge `feature/directory-hub` into main. It also carries `feature/directory-regions`, which isn't on main yet.
2. Deploy through the existing script, not a raw build: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` on the branch, then `promote-production.sh`. There's no migration.
3. Check that `/sitemap/3.xml` returns 404 and `/game-servers/directory` looks as it does today.
4. To turn it on, flip "New directory pages (v2)" on `/admin/directory`. It's read per request, so no restart is needed.
5. Check `/game-servers/directory/rust`, `/game-servers/directory/rust/germany`, a `/server/<id>` page and `/sitemap/directory.xml`. The index picks up the new section within 5 minutes (sitemap cache).
6. To roll back, flip the flag off.
